sections.model_projection: The model projects Indianapolis 24.44, Baltimore 22.03, a home margin of 2.41 points. The projected total is 46.47, sitting just under the market total of 47.5. Indianapolis is given a 55.7% win probability, while the market's no-vig implied probability actually favors Baltimore at 60.9%, representing a notable divergence. The model's margin of 2.41 points leans meaningfully toward the Colts compared to the market spread of Indianapolis -3.5.
sections.offensive_matchup: Indianapolis holds a clear overall offensive edge, ranking 6th in EPA per play (a measure of how many expected points each play generates) at 0.096 versus Baltimore's 0.057 ranked 12th. The Colts also rank 7th in offensive success rate at 46.7%, meaning nearly half their plays generate positive expected value, compared to Baltimore's 45.6%. Indianapolis's rushing attack is particularly potent, ranking 3rd in rushing EPA per play at 0.058, while Baltimore's run defense ranks 8th in rushing EPA allowed, setting up a competitive but Colts-favored ground game. Baltimore's defense ranks 22nd in overall EPA allowed per play and 22nd in yards allowed per play at 5.62, suggesting Indianapolis should find consistent yardage.
sections.quarterback_edge: Lamar Jackson carries a significant career EPA per dropback of +0.108, ranking among the league's elite, while Daniel Jones sits at -0.029 career EPA per dropback, meaning his dropbacks have historically cost his team expected points on average. Jackson has attempted 2,045 career passes at 8.01 yards per attempt with a 65.2% completion rate and a 126-to-40 touchdown-to-interception ratio across 72 games. Jones has completed 65.8% of his passes but at only 6.82 yards per attempt with a 56-to-34 ratio across 56 games. This quarterback edge is the single largest factor favoring Baltimore in the model, worth approximately 0.74 points toward the Ravens.
sections.trenches: The offensive line edge favors Indianapolis, which ranks 7th in sack rate allowed at 4.8% and 9th in pressure rate allowed at 19.2%, while Baltimore's pass rush ranks 31st in sack rate at 4.3% and 29th in pressure rate at 18.7%. That mismatch in pass protection versus pass rush is the primary driver of the offensive line edge going to the Colts. On run blocking, Baltimore's defensive line yards allowed rank 7th at 2.73 yards credited to the offensive line per rush, while Indianapolis's offensive line yards rank 19th at 2.81, making the run-blocking matchup closer to neutral. Baltimore's own offensive line allowed a sack rate of 8.95%, ranking 27th, which could be a problem against Indianapolis's pass rush that generates pressure on 24.2% of dropbacks.
sections.explosive_play_edge: Baltimore holds a slight edge in the explosive play category, generating big plays (10-plus rushing or 20-plus passing yards) on 10.3% of their offensive plays, ranking 6th, compared to Indianapolis's 7.8% rate ranked 23rd. However, Baltimore's defense allows explosive plays on 10.1% of opponent plays, ranking 26th, while Indianapolis allows them on 9.1%, ranking 19th. The net result is essentially a wash, with Baltimore's ability to create explosives partially offset by their vulnerability to giving them up. Indianapolis's play-action rate of 29.7% (ranked 5th) against Baltimore's pressure-without-blitz rate of just 10.3% (ranked 29th) could generate chunk plays for the Colts when they use pre-snap motion to stress the defense.
sections.third_down_red_zone: Baltimore holds a meaningful third-down edge: their defense allows opponents to convert only 38.2% of third downs (ranked 10th), while Indianapolis's defense allows 43.1% (ranked 25th), meaning Baltimore's defense is significantly better at getting off the field. Indianapolis converts 43.5% of their own third downs (ranked 7th), but they face a Ravens defense that has been above average at limiting conversions. In the red zone, Indianapolis scores touchdowns on 64.5% of trips (ranked 10th) against a Baltimore defense that allows touchdowns on only 49.2% of red-zone visits (ranked 3rd), creating a genuine tension between Indianapolis's red-zone offense and Baltimore's red-zone defense. Baltimore's own red-zone offense converts at just 56.5% (ranked 21st), though they face an Indianapolis defense that allows touchdowns on 52.5% of red-zone trips (ranked 6th).
sections.roster_talent: Insufficient reliable data for NFL talent ratings. Indianapolis shows a notably higher roster continuity index at 0.86 versus Baltimore's 0.68, and the Colts have not changed their head coach while Baltimore has, giving Indianapolis a familiarity advantage worth approximately 0.57 points in the model. Indianapolis also returns 94% of their rushing production and 83% of passing production, while Baltimore returns 88% of passing and 87% of rushing production but with a lower overall continuity score of 0.68. The returning production edge favors Indianapolis and contributes approximately 0.33 points toward the Colts in the model.

sections.expected_game_script: Indianapolis figures to establish the run early, leveraging their 3rd-ranked rushing EPA offense against a Baltimore run defense that ranks 8th but faces a Colts offensive line that protects well. Daniel Jones will likely lean on play-action heavily at a 29.7% rate to create favorable passing situations, particularly since Baltimore generates very little pressure without blitzing (ranked 29th at 10.3%). Baltimore will counter with Lamar Jackson's dual-threat ability, and his career 8.01 yards per attempt should stress an Indianapolis pass defense ranked 21st in passing EPA allowed. The Ravens' run-heavy identity (ranked last in pass rate at 52.5% and 30th in neutral-script pass rate) means they will try to control tempo with a slow pace (ranked 30th in seconds per play), which could keep the game close and low-scoring. Baltimore's red-zone defense (ranked 3rd in touchdown rate allowed) may force Indianapolis to settle for field goals on some drives, keeping the Ravens within striking distance despite the offensive disadvantage. The most likely outcome is a competitive, relatively low-scoring game that stays within a possession throughout the fourth quarter, with Indianapolis's home-field advantage and offensive efficiency giving them a slight edge to close it out.
